A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same STree research and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. v1's Appendix A is retained, and v2 adds Appendices B and C. No material reading gaps prevent comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original measurements of latency, generation speed, memory use, and token acceptance, including benchmark comparisons and ablations in Section 5.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds model-size timing, draft-checkpoint, H100, and dynamic-tree results.

M1.justification: The tree-mask construction, accumulated state transitions, tree-scan kernel, activation replay, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. Beam-search drafting already appears in v1 Section 5.1; its additional hybrid-model evaluation does not introduce a new STree procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use MT-Bench, HumanEval, and GSM8K for the same generation tasks and describe the same distillation data source. Added hardware, model-size, and drafting tests vary experimental settings without adding datasets or task requirements.

E2.justification: v2 Appendix C/Table 8 newly compares beam-search and static-tree STree directly in hybrid-model generation; v1 evaluates beam search in the pure-Mamba packed-versus-unrolled comparison. The new model-size latency table also includes an autoregressive reference alongside vanilla SD. Existing FSS, Chunk Scan, and generation baselines are retained.

E3.justification: v2 substantially extends evaluation settings with H100 execution, randomly initialized 7B/13B/23B models for latency measurement, draft checkpoints at 12,000/48,000/264,000 steps, and hybrid-model greedy beam-search drafting with M=3 and N=4. These are added protocols; the original RTX 3090 experiments and their stated settings remain.

E4.justification: New analyses test how relative overhead varies with model size, how draft training affects acceptance and speed, whether gains persist on H100, and whether dynamic trees improve hybrid generation. These substantially broaden sensitivity and applicability evidence beyond the retained temperature, sampling, static-tree, and transformer-proportion ablations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty estimates for the performance measurements. The added experiments retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: v1 Tables 1–4 retain identical numerical content as v2 Tables 2–5, and the original plotted results are unchanged. v2 Tables 1, 6, 7, and 8 add substantial results. For example, H100 MT-Bench throughput is 113.13 versus 113.60 tokens/s for STree versus vanilla SD under greedy generation, but 85.18 versus 80.76 at temperature 1. The new hybrid beam-tree comparison reports 71.60 versus 69.84 tokens/s for beam versus static drafting.

T1.justification: The tree-mask definitions, accumulated-transition derivation, and runtime inequalities are retained. v2 displays the D(u_t)u_t output term in Equation 1, but v1 already describes it in prose; v2 explicitly omits it for the unchanged derivation. No new proof or substantive mathematical argument is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion retain the same central contributions: scalable speculative tree decoding for SSMs and hybrids, a hardware-aware implementation, runtime–acceptance analysis, and speed improvements using simple drafting. Additional experiments support these claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations linking H100's smaller gains and greedy slowdowns to memory bandwidth and relative overhead, while noting the kernels are not H100-optimized. It also interprets checkpoint improvements through draft–target alignment and conditions larger-model benefits on maintained acceptance length. These extend the existing runtime–acceptance interpretation and applicability qualifications.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces a promise of code release after acceptance with a repository address. Added experiments disclose checkpoint steps, random initialization of large models, H100 use, and beam parameters. Conversely, v1's explicit statement that A and B are discretized by delta is omitted. The PDFs establish these documentation changes, not the contents of the linked repository.

R1.justification: v2 newly cites B'mojo when discussing input-dependent SSM parameters. The removed ICML reference to Leviathan et al. duplicates the retained preprint of the same work, so it is not removal of a distinct cited contribution. The overall novelty positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized wording corrections, removes a repeated novelty paragraph, and adds headings for new analyses and appendices while preserving the main narrative order. Conference, correspondence, and acknowledgment text is added. An unresolved speculative-sampling citation and an incorrect Appendix C table cross-reference are introduced.

P2.justification: Four new tables substantially expand the displayed evidence: model-size latency, checkpoint sensitivity, H100 comparisons, and static-versus-beam drafting. All five original figures retain their graphics, while Algorithm 1 and several figures and tables are relocated as the main text and appendices accommodate the additions.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's RTX 3090 evaluations, v2 provides useful hardware and drafting sensitivity evidence, including H100 cases where STree loses to vanilla SD, and supplies a code address. These additions improve practical assessment. The gain is limited by incompletely specified new settings, random-weight-only large-model timing, and inconsistent checkpoint percentages: Table 6's 42.96 versus 44.52 tokens/s implies about 3.5% slower performance, not the stated 1%.
